signal: EliseAI raised a $250M Series E at a $2.2B valuation and plans to double headcount to 600 across housing and healthcare

email.body1:
Jack, saw EliseAI closed a $250M Series E at a $2.2B valuation and is doubling the team toward 600.

Scaling that fast means more accounts and inbound than any SDR can follow up on by hand, and slow follow-up is where replies get left on the table. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and runs multi-channel follow-up autonomously, so output scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I had our AI SDR draft three personalized emails to three accounts that fit your motion. Want to hop on a quick call and I'll walk you through them?
email.body2:
Jack, quick follow-up for EliseAI.

When volume spikes the bottleneck is usually research and writing time per prospect, not effort, so response speed slips and ramp drags. That is fixable without adding reps, and the lift tends to show up fast once the busywork is off your plate.

Worth 15 minutes? I'll walk you through a teardown of your current outbound, three things I'd change, and our best practices alone usually lift response rates 50 to 70%.
email.body3:
Jack, last bit of proof for EliseAI.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how EliseAI's reply rate likely compares to other fast-scaling AI teams. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Jack, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If taking follow-up volume off your plate without adding headcount isn't a priority right now, no problem at all. Doubling the team is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your SDR motion? I'll tailor it to EliseAI either way.
